english.title: Aid / abet driving a motor vehicle whilst disqualified
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) aided, abetted, counselled and procured **(..SPECIFY NAME OF DISQUALIFIED PERSON..) a person disqualified from holding or obtaining a driving licence, to drive a motor vehicle, namely **(..SPECIFY VEHICLE MAKE AND INDEX NUMBER..), on a road, namely **(..SPECIFY ROAD AND LOCATION..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section103(1)(b) of the Road Traffic Act 1988, section 44 of the Magistrates'Courts Act 1980 and Schedule 2 to the Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required

english.notes: This offence wording does NOT APPLY to disqualification by virtue of section 101 (disqualification by reason of age - see offence wording H372), nor in relation to disqualification by virtue of section 102 of the Road traffic act 1988 (duplicate licences).

other.penalty:
Summary : Six months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Discretionary disqualification

Obligatory endorsement - licence endorsed six penalty points.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
